description: Card describing a signed-in device: icon (decorative), label, optional "Current device" badge, vendor/model, user agent, last seen, IP, country and first seen. With onRevoke, and only when the device isn't the current one, a Revoke button sits on the right.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the Revoke button, when there is one.

focus.notes: The Revoke button uses the browser's default focus outline. While revokePending is true it's disabled and leaves the tab order, so focus is lost; move it somewhere sensible when the request settles.

announcements: Reads the label, the badge text, then the metadata lines in order.
The button reads revokeLabel ("Revoke") only, without the device name.
screenReader.notes: In a list of devices every button reads "Revoke". Pass a revokeLabel that names the device, or render the cards in a list with a heading per device, so the action is unambiguous.

contrast.text: Label in text-card-foreground and metadata in text-muted-foreground pass 4.5:1. Known issue: the "Current device" badge uses text-primary on a 15% primary tint, about 2.3:1 with the orange primary on cream; it doesn't meet 4.5:1 for small text.
contrast.ui: The Revoke button's destructive border is decorative; its text-destructive label passes 4.5:1 on the light tint.

motion.reducedMotion: Only a background-color transition on the Revoke button.

consumerResponsibilities: Give each Revoke button a device-specific accessible name (revokeLabel such as "Revoke Chrome on Windows").
Confirm before revoking, and announce the result (for example with a toast).
Pass formatDate for localized dates; the default uses toLocaleDateString().
